questions.question: Which of these is a proposition?
questions.explanation: A proposition has a definite truth value. "x > 5" has a free variable; questions and commands are not truth-valued.

questions.question: In Python, P → Q (material implication) is written…
questions.explanation: Implication is false only when P is true and Q is false — exactly the truth table of (not P) or Q.

questions.question: A truth table over n variables has how many rows?
questions.explanation: Each variable is independently true or false: 2 × 2 × … × 2 = 2ⁿ possible assignments.

questions.question: "If it rains, the ground is wet" and "if the ground is wet, it rained" are…
options: a statement and its converse — different claims
questions.explanation: The second is the converse. A sprinkler makes the ground wet without rain — the lesson's counterexample.

questions.question: Two compound statements are logically equivalent when…
options: they have identical truth values under every assignment
questions.explanation: Equivalence means same truth table column — same value in every possible world.

questions.question: When is the promise P → Q broken?
options: P is false and Q is false
P is true and Q is false
P is false and Q is true
questions.explanation: A promise is only violated when its premise held and the conclusion failed. F → anything is vacuously true.

questions.question: De Morgan's laws state that ¬(P ∨ Q) equals…
questions.explanation: Negation flips ∨ to ∧ and negates each part — proven by cases in the lesson, checked by truth table.

questions.question: The contrapositive of P → Q is…
questions.explanation: Flip and negate both. The contrapositive is always equivalent to the original — unlike the converse.

questions.question: Why is brute-force truth-table checking a complete proof for propositional formulas?
options: Because a formula over n variables has only 2ⁿ possible worlds — finite subject matter
It is not a proof; it is only evidence
questions.explanation: Exhausting all 2ⁿ assignments leaves no world unchecked. Over infinite domains enumeration loses this power.

questions.question: A billing rule reads `not (expired or unpaid)`. An equivalent rewrite is…
questions.explanation: De Morgan: the negation distributes inward and flips or to and — the exact example from the lesson opening.

questions.question: How many logically distinct binary connectives exist (truth functions on two inputs)?
questions.explanation: A binary connective fills a 4-row truth table, each row T or F: 2⁴ = 16. The lesson script counts them.
